newsitem.title: GERMANY: Vereinsbank raises Siemens to overweight.
newsitem.headline: Vereinsbank raises Siemens to overweight.

text.p: Germany's Vereinsbank said on Friday it has raised its rating on electronics group Siemens AG to overweight from neutral.

Vereinsbank analyst Thilo Hasler said in a report that he expected "above-average development" in Siemens shares over the medium-term, in part due to the Munich-based group's strategic acquisition policy.

Halser, also noting market hopes that Siemen's operating profit margins would improve, said he raised profit forecasts to 1995/96 business year to 4.66 marks per share from 4.45 marks and 1997/98 to 5.77 marks from 5.20 marks.
He also targeted Siemens shares to reach 100 marks.
Siemens shares were up 83 pfennigs at 86.12 marks in pre-bourse IBIS dealings, outpacing the broader market where the IBIS DAX was up 9.11 points at 3,133.89 points.
Traders also said on Friday that Dresdner Bank AG has raised its recommendation on German electronics giant Siemens AG to buy from hold.
"The recommendation has been changed to buy from hold," said one trader who asked not to be named.
Dresdner Bank's analyst for Siemens was not immediately available for comment.
